absent: Numeric values of control register bits, feature indices, leaf numbers, table sizes and register encodings.
Field layouts of processor info and device and matching and descriptor and enumeration leaf records.
Implementation of safe register access, matching, printing, percpu access, branch and assertion helpers.
Call order and timing of detection, capability, protection and table setup during boot and hotplug.
Contents of vendor device tables, scattered bit descriptions, legacy model tables and forced capability masks.
Synchronization beyond the interrupt disabled requirement for shadow updates.
Error paths for failed descriptor loads, failed hotplug registration and missing vendor hooks.

findings.text: Control register store routines for two registers plus a shadow synchronizer and an early initializer are globally visible for other setup paths to call.
Direct and fixed mapping table loaders plus the early combined table and per processor base switch are globally visible for boot sequencing.
Vendor resolver and basic detector plus capability collector and translation cache reporter and identifier flag probe are globally visible for bring up.
A small record groups one capability index with two register selectors for control and data. A vendor indexed table holds one instance per supported vendor.
A dependent capability record pairs a feature index with a required enumeration level, both as fixed width integers. Its table ends with a zero entry.
Seven mostly read counters track last level instruction and data translation entries by page size, covering small and large pages including a very large data page.
A per processor pointer refers to the entry area for the current processor, allowing each processor to reach its own entry state.
The package thread count starts at one and becomes immutable after initialization completes.

Generic initialization detects cache sizes on one build and labels very old processors without enumeration on the other. The current selector starts at a generic Unknown device until vendor matching replaces it.
Two early options reject any argument, stay silent when the boot processor lacks the associated second level translation capability, otherwise withdraw the capability and log once.

Flag mutability is probed by toggling the requested bit through stack operations on one build and is always reported true on the other. Identifier availability is derived from the identifier bit probe.
Cache size override starts negative meaning no override and its option parses an integer from the command line. Serial number suppression starts enabled and its option clears that suppression.
Two supervisor protections are enabled in the control register only when the current processor advertises them, with the access protection path asserting that a user access flag is already clear.

User instruction restriction is enabled only when both the boot processor plus build gates and the current processor allow it, with a single log on success, and is otherwise explicitly cleared to remove residue from a prior boot.

Protected identifier bring up matches the processor against a table, safely reads control, abandons when access fails or control shows locked off, tries to turn enablement on when off and rereads, then on enabled captures the identifier and advertises support else withdraws support.
Matching covers feature based entries for two vendors plus many legacy model entries that lack enumeration, all pointing at the vendor appropriate control description.

Pinning snapshots the current shadow restricted to a fixed mask during early init and arms enforcement. Later stores rewrite any drift back to the snapshot and emit a one time warning, with one register guarding write protect and the other guarding the mask.

Early control register initialization starts from hardware state, adds second level translation enablement when the boot processor supports it, reapplies pinned bits when enforcement is armed, then writes hardware and refreshes the per processor shadow.
Early command line entries handle translation identifiers and base register control plus key protection and serial number and cache size; they run before processor bring up completes.
The base register option requires an empty argument, reports success without action when the boot processor lacks the feature, otherwise withdraws the feature and logs.

Key protection bring up on the boot processor honors a disable flag and build plus hardware gates before forcing the operating system capability, while later processors gate only on that forced capability, then all set the control bit and load a default rights value.

Enforcement technology bring up evaluates build gates and kernel versus user desires, advertises user shadow stack when wanted, programs supervisor state to enable or zero, sets the control bit, then self tests the kernel path and unwinds supervisor state plus the kernel capability on failure.
Teardown clears both supervisor and user enforcement states, but does nothing unless either kernel branch protection or user shadow stack was enabled.

The X86_FEATURE_MWAIT capability together with the X86_FEATURE_DCA capability together with the X86_FEATURE_XSAVE capability is withdrawn when the current maximum level is below the required leaf, with signed handling that differs between standard and extended maxima, optionally warning with the capability name and leaf.
Legacy model naming on one build range checks the model index and walks a vendor table for a family match, returning no name when out of range or unmatched or on the other build.
Both table loaders build a descriptor from the per processor table base with length one less than the table size, differing only in read write versus read only source.

Early switch first loads the direct table, then on one build writes the kernel base register while preserving segment state and on the other reloads the per processor segment, discarding any early per processor content that was not copied.
Vendor resolution scans registered devices comparing up to two identification strings, adopting the first match and otherwise falling back to generic with a single instability error.

Model identification requires a minimum extended level, gathers three leaves into a fixed length buffer with termination, then strips leading blanks and trims trailing blanks by tracking the last significant character.
Basic detection defaults the family to four, copies vendor text from the first leaf, then when the second leaf exists derives family plus model plus stepping and scales flush size into alignment.
Translation cache discovery delegates to a vendor hook when present, then logs instruction counts by three page sizes and data counts by four page sizes.

Capability collection samples standard and thermal and extended state leaves plus several extended leaves, merges scattered bits and speculation synthesis and fast system call synthesis, then applies forced set and clear masks on every reprobe.
Scattered harvesting walks a bit description table, validates each entry level against the current maximum range, samples the indicated subleaf and sets the feature when the indicated bit is present.

Speculation synthesis expands generic control into branch mitigations plus register control, mirrors vendor specific controls into the same outputs, derives stop predictions from either of two inputs, and drops the virtual stop bit when the direct stop bit is present.
Forced capabilities are reapplied after each probe by clearing masked bits and setting forced bits across capability plus bug words.
A tiny assembly entry saves processor flags to the return register, and a separate assembly entry exercises indirect branch protection by jumping through a loaded address.

A per processor enable routine sets the address space protection bit, registered as a dynamic hotplug step that runs on all current and future online processors when the feature is enabled, otherwise finalization does nothing.
Shadow control register updates require interrupts disabled, verified by assertion, and combine per processor shadow plus hardware write only when the computed value differs.
Access protection setup treats a set user access flag as a fatal state error, so callers must ensure that flag was cleared much earlier.

One build variant touches a configuration register to suppress the serial number, clears the associated capability and refreshes the maximum level, while the other variant does nothing, so behavior differs by build.
Stores that attempt to clear pinned bits do not fail; they are corrected back and only warn once, which can hide caller errors if warnings are ignored.
Unknown vendor identification falls back to generic operation after a single error noting possible instability, so later vendor specific hooks may be missing.
Stale enablement from a previous boot is explicitly cleared when current gates do not allow the feature, preventing unintended carry over across reboot mechanisms.
The pinned mask combines X86_CR4_SMEP together with X86_CR4_SMAP together with X86_CR4_UMIP together with X86_CR4_FSGSBASE together with X86_CR4_CET.
